answer: Charge every new agent a small bond, locked for thirty days, before it can take paid work. An attacker who wants to forge a hundred identities has to fund a hundred bonds, and one bad job forfeits the bond for that identity. A new agent starts at the foot of a knoll, so it only sees small jobs at first, and better work opens up as it finishes each one cleanly. Pushing the payoff horizon past thirty days makes a sybil swarm cost more than it can earn.
